text: Ten lessons ago, this project started with one frustrated sentence from Jaffle Shop's Ops Manager: our customer data is a mess, I just want ONE list I can trust. This final lesson recaps everything that sentence turned into, pulls out the real skills underneath the tools, and looks ahead to what's next.

Lesson one turned the complaint into a specific requirement. Lesson two planned the project in three layers before building anything. Lessons three through five got the raw data into Snowflake, scaffolded the dbt project, and declared the source. Lessons six through nine built the staging model, wrote real tests, built the mart model, and ran the whole project end to end with a clean dbt build.

None of these lessons were really about dbt or Snowflake syntax alone. Lesson one was requirements clarification. Lessons two, five, and six were about disciplined, minimal layering — doing exactly one job per layer, no more. And lesson seven turned a vague promise into testable trust — not a feeling, a passing automated check. A hiring manager cares about this far more than which command you typed.

This project was scoped smaller than the full capstone sequence on purpose. No order history, no payment totals, no intermediate models, no CI/CD, no production scheduling. That wasn't a limitation to apologize for — it was the correct scope for the actual request, and knowing how to scope down is as real a skill as knowing how to scope up.

The next project in this sequence raises the stakes in exactly the direction this one avoided. raw_orders and raw_payments join in alongside raw_customers, an intermediate layer appears for the first time, and the mart model finally stops looking like a pass-through of staging and starts doing real business logic.

The skills from this project don't get replaced in that next one — requirements clarification, the sources, staging, marts discipline, and real dbt tests are still the foundation. They just get applied to a harder, more ambiguous ask, with more real tables involved. Congratulations on finishing the Beginner Capstone — on to Intermediate next.
